preconditions.description: Input consists of exactly two lines: the string s on the first line and integer k on the second line.
The first line (string s) contains only lowercase Latin letters.
The length of string s is between 1 and 1000 (inclusive).
The integer k is between 1 and 26 (inclusive).

postconditions.description: Output is either the word 'impossible' or a non-negative integer representing the minimum number of changes required, which cannot exceed the length of s.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'impossible' if int(stdin.splitlines()[1]) > len(stdin.splitlines()[0]) else True
postconditions.description: If k exceeds the length of s, output is 'impossible' because it's impossible to have k distinct letters in a string shorter than k.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '0' if len(set(stdin.splitlines()[0])) >= int(stdin.splitlines()[1]) else True
postconditions.description: If the number of distinct letters in s is already >= k, output is '0' (no changes needed).

postconditions.expression: (stdout.strip() != 'impossible' and int(stdout.strip()) == min(len(stdin.splitlines()[0]) - len(set(stdin.splitlines()[0])), int(stdin.splitlines()[1]) - len(set(stdin.splitlines()[0])))) if len(set(stdin.splitlines()[0])) < int(stdin.splitlines()[1]) <= len(stdin.splitlines()[0]) else True
postconditions.description: If k is achievable (i.e., k <= len(s) and k > current distinct letters), output is the minimum number of changes required, which is the smaller of (len(s) - current_distinct) or (k - current_distinct).
